title: Single-molecule tracking for studying protein dynamics and target-search mechanism in live cells of S. cerevisiae
protocol: Streak yeast cells from the −80°C freezer onto a SC+Agar plate for single colonies.
Incubate the plate at 30°C for 2 days.
Inoculate a single colony in 3 mL SC broth in a 14 mL Falcon tube.
Grow cells at 30°C at 230 RPM for 20–24 hours for saturated growth.
Inoculate 50 μL of the saturated culture into fresh 3 mL of SC media in a 14 mL Falcon tube.
Grow cells at 30°C at 230 RPM for 4–5 hours to bring them to the log phase of growth.
Centrifuge 3 mL culture to pellet down the cells (∼ 541 × g for 1 minute).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of fresh prewarmed SC media.
Add fluorescently labeled HTL.
Shake the culture for an additional 30 min after adding the HTL at 30°C at 230 RPM.
Centrifuge the culture (541 × g for 1 min) to pellet down the cells.
Discard the supernatant gently.
Wash the cells twice or thrice with prewarmed SC media (1 ml each wash, 541 × g for 1 min).
Resuspend the cells in the remaining 10–20 μL of media.
Take 3 μL of this cell suspension for imaging.
Add 250 mg of SeaKem GTG Agarose to 25 mL of SC media in a 100 mL flask.
Boil the mixture in a microwave until all agarose particles dissolve.
Mix well and boil again.
Pour exactly 15 mL of the media into a 100 mm Petri dish.
Let it solidify (∼20 min).
Keep the lid of the petri dish open for 20 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Prepare the agarose pad freshly just before imaging.
Turn on the microscope software and hardware.
Turn on the stage incubator at 30°C.
Leave the stage incubator on for 30 minutes before imaging for temperature stabilization.
Take a LabTek II chamber with a 1.5 mm cover glass.
Put 3 μL of cell suspension from step no. 10 into the chamber.
Cut an 8 mm × 8 mm agarose slab from the Petri dish using a surgical blade.
Place the agarose slab upside down on top of the cell suspension.
Gently press the agarose pad with a finger or the back of a pipette tip to spread the cells evenly and arrange them in monolayer.
Close the lid of the LabTek II chamber.
Focus on the cells under the microscope using a 100× 1.49 NA oil objective lens, in transmitted light mode.
Find the best field for imaging with approximately 10–20 cells in monolayer.
Switch the transmitted light mode to fluorescence mode/reflected light mode.
Switch on the 488 laser to focus on the intracellular structure/protein labeled with GFP.
Set acquisition parameters in the imaging software.
Adjust the power of the 488 nm laser to clearly visualize GFP-labelled protein/structure in a single-focal plane.
Adjust the power of the 647 nm laser to make single molecules of -HaloTag protein visible.
Select a field with approximately 10–20 cells per image.
Adjust the 488-laser power so that the entire nucleus is visible in a single-focal plane.
Adjust the 647-laser power such that single-molecules of Hht1 are visible with a signal-to-noise ratio of at least 5:1.
Optimize laser power for single-molecule visibility with a signal to noise ratio of approximately 5:1.
Reduce laser power proportionally when using long exposure times.
Use an exposure time between 10–30 ms for quantifying diffusion parameters such as MSD, diffusion coefficient, bound and unbound molecules, and target-search mechanism.
For residence time quantification, use a higher exposure time of ∼200–500 ms with low laser power to capture only the bound molecules.
Do not perform z-stack imaging due to technical limitations such as fast photobleaching and reduced imaging speed.
Acquire images for single-molecule tracking at different time intervals.
Capture ∼1,000–2,000 frames in continuous acquisition mode (10–30 ms exposure, 0 min time interval) until seeing a negligible number of single molecules.
Acquire ∼200–400 frames for long time-lapse imaging with time intervals of 200 ms, 500 ms, 750 ms, or 1,000 ms until observing a negligible number of single molecules.
Ensure acquisition parameters yield at least 1,000 tracks per strain or condition.
Prepare an imaging session of 4–5 hours per day to collect movies.
Collect 20 movies for each time interval: 0 ms (1,000 frames), 200 ms (200 frames), and 1,000 ms (100 frames).
Acquire approximately 30 to 50 movies to obtain 1,000 tracks.
Complete one experiment in 2–3 days with imaging sessions of 4–5 hours daily.
Do not image cells from the same agarose pad for longer than 1 hour to avoid phototoxicity artifacts.
Take freshly growing cells and place a new agarose pad in the LabTekII chamber every 1 hour.
Save all movies as .tiff files.
